question: Knowing what is known at the review date, would we write materially different protections for this borrower?

evidence_attributable_changes.rationale: The company expects to need additional time to prepare historical and pro forma financial statements after the VIP acquisition, indicating potential difficulty meeting the 90‑day deadline.
evidence_attributable_changes.change: Extend the deadline for delivering annual financial statements and Compliance Certificate beyond the current 90‑day period after fiscal year end.

evidence.quote: The preparation process is ongoing and the Company expects to have this work completed within the allotted 75 day period following the close of the transaction.

updated_summary: Evidence indicates the borrower may need extra time to prepare annual financial statements post‑acquisition, justifying a loosened reporting deadline. No other covenant requires change.
updated_reasons: Evidence of needed extra time for annual financial statements justifies a loosened reporting permission, altering permitted behavior and thus constituting material drift.
reading: Changes listed as evidence-attributable appear only when the new reports are supplied. Changes also present in the control reflect pre-existing gaps or model drafting preference, not newly emerging drift. One run of each; repeat-run stability is not yet measured.
